title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: logged-in user email on the Windows device onboarding page (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its government-cloud release facts, client prerequisite, licensing and documented read and role-assignment routes are supported. Minor corrections should flag conflicting Microsoft permissions guidance, cite the PowerShell reference and classify this existing-page enhancement as prepare rather than review.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn lists Anti-malware Client Version 4.18.26030 or newer as the logged-in user details prerequisite under roadmap ID 548669.
claims.quote: Logged-in user details (user email) on the device onboarding page (Roadmap ID 548669) | Anti-malware Client Version 4.18.26030 or newer is required.

claims.quote: Windows 10: See update details Windows 11 22H2: See update details Windows 11 23H2: See update details Windows 11 24H2: See update details

claims.claim: Learn does not explain the new email field's placement or display mechanics beyond the prerequisite entry.
claims.quote: Searched: "logged-in user" "device onboarding" "email"; read device-onboarding-overview and dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync. Found the prerequisite row and existing device attributes, not a description of the new field's rendering.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices reaches the device list used to read device status and attributes.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" is a documented KQL read query for Endpoint DLP device data.
claims.quote: Sample query: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" | project DlpInfo

claims.claim: The DeviceInfo query runs in Advanced hunting in the Microsoft Defender portal.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Defender portal. Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting. Query the DeviceInfo table.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo's DlpInfo column contains Endpoint DLP device properties, including DlpUpn.
claims.quote: The DlpInfo column contains Endpoint Data Loss Prevention device information in JSON format. The following properties can be returned in the DlpInfo object: ... DlpUpn

claims.claim: DlpUpn is the user principal name associated with the device.
claims.quote: DlpUpn | string | User principal name (UPN) associated with the device.

claims.claim: Learn says DlpInfo values correspond to information on the DLP device onboarding page.
claims.quote: These values correspond to the device information available in the DLP device onboarding page.

claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "DlpUpn" "logged-in" roles email; read dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync and device-onboarding-overview. The former defines a device-associated UPN, without explicitly mapping it to the new email field.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Device management access is governed by Entra role assignments rather than Purview roles.
claims.quote: Device management currently only supports Entra roles. Purview roles are not supported.
claims.fix: Retain the attribution to the onboarding overview, and add: 'Microsoft's roles reference also lists the Purview View-Only Device Management role as allowing viewing of Device Management configuration and reports; the pages do not agree on role support.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/scc-permissions#roles-in-microsoft-defender-for-office-365-and-microsoft-purview.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn requires a custom account viewing device management settings to have one of Compliance admin, Compliance data admin, Global reader, Security admin or Global admin.
claims.quote: If you want to use a custom account to view the device management settings, it must be in one of these roles: Compliance admin; Compliance data admin; Global reader; Security admin; Global admin

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope: Roles; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not separately specify whether each listed device-settings role sees the new email field.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "DlpUpn" "logged-in" roles email; "logged-in user" "device onboarding" "email". Read onboarding Permissions and the feature row; no field-specific permission distinction is stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes no new permission specifically for the logged-in user detail.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "DlpUpn" "logged-in" roles email; read device-onboarding-overview Permissions and feature prerequisites, and dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync. No new email-field permission is documented.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Roles & admins > role > Add assignments is the documented tenant-scope role-assignment route.
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Roles & admins. Select a role name to open the role. ... Select Add assignments and then select the users, groups, or agent identities you want to assign to this role.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments assigns an Entra directory role.
claims.quote: Use the Create unifiedRoleAssignment API to assign the role. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.claim: The role-assignment request body uses principalId and roleDefinitionId to identify the assignee and role.
claims.quote: "principalId": "<Object ID of user or group>", "roleDefinitionId": "<ID of role definition>", "directoryScopeId": "/"

claims.claim: Assigning tenant-scope Entra roles requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Privileged Role Administrator.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: A switch to show or hide the logged-in user detail is not documented on either the admin UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "device onboarding" "user" "email" "hide"; "device onboarding" "logged-in" Graph API PowerShell show user details; logged-in user details hide show Set-PolicyConfig. Read onboarding overview, troubleshooting and Set-PolicyConfig syntax; no switch found.

claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "device onboarding" "user email" "default"; read roadmap 559028, onboarding overview and troubleshooting. The record says admins can now see the user, but no source specifies default enablement or an enabling action for this field.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe rollout mechanics for this email display beyond the roadmap's status and target.
claims.quote: Searched: "logged-in user details" licensing pricing meter default rollout permissions DlpUpn; "Purview" "device onboarding" "user email" "default". Read roadmap and onboarding overview; no feature-specific deployment sequence or release-channel mechanics found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap describes an administrator-facing information display, not an automated action on devices or an end-user workflow change.
claims.quote: This update introduces logged-in user details (user email) on the device onboarding page for Windows devices ... Admins can now see which user is currently signed in on a device

claims.claim: The review action rating treats this existing-page enhancement as an optional capability.
claims.quote: action: "review"; summary: "The Purview device onboarding page shows the signed-in user's email for Windows devices"; Why it matters: "the practical work is small: confirm that Windows devices meet the client prerequisite"
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare': the standard assigns prepare to enhancements of an existing experience that arrive anyway and need low-risk checks or communication, including when the default state is unknown.
